title: Postmortem: restore tenant correlation across console traces & synthetic ingress heartbeats
creator: Aisha Martínez
description:
Summary: During a capacity regression on 2026-03-04 a spike in console ingress queues and subsequent KV evictions were not attributable to tenants in our dashboards or traces. This produced a blind spot: on-call could not isolate the spike to a single customer or workload, delaying mitigations and prolonging elevated latency for ~37 minutes.

Detection & Impact: The alerting alarm for 95th ingress queue depth fired at 2026-03-04T02:11Z. Operators saw increased retries and tail latency but dashboards lacked tenant-level percentiles and traces were missing the tenant correlation header, so escalation required broad throttles and a temporary global capacity scale-up. Customer-facing errors were limited (rate-limited routes), but internal costs and latency SLO violations occurred.

Root cause: Two simultaneous regressions: (1) a recent routing proxy change introduced a header size limit causing the x-rd-tenant-id propagation to be dropped when additional debug headers were present in batched requests; (2) the synthetic "ingress-heartbeat" job was disabled during a metrics-config rollout so there was no synthetic signal to reconcile dashboards. The trace aggregator also sampled-out many short-lived spans due to a sampling cliff introduced in a prior change. Together these removed both correlation metadata and a synthetic baseline metric.

Mitigation performed during incident: Re-enabled conservative header passthrough policy (rollback of proxy change) at 02:28Z which restored tenant headers for new requests, re-enabled the heartbeat job at 02:35Z. Scaling knobs were used to reduce tail latency until tenant correlation was restored.

Action items (this ticket):
  1) Add a trace-propagation contract test that validates x-rd-tenant-id survives batching + debug headers. Owner: Liam O'Connor. Estimate: 3.
  2) Re-introduce tenant-labelled synthetic ingress-heartbeats and add an alert for lost heartbeats per-tenant. Owner: Priya Desai. Estimate: 2.
  3) Implement an aggregator-side defensive check: if tenant header missing but synthetic heartbeat exists mark trace with "recovered-tenant" and emit metric for investigation. Owner: Backend Observability. Estimate: 2.
  4) Dashboard work: add tenant percentile (p50/p95/p99) for ingress queue depth and KV eviction rate; annotate runbook links. Owner: Console UX. Estimate: 3.
  5) Sampling policy review: probe and adjust sampling cliff thresholds for short-lived spans to avoid blindspot windows. Owner: Tracing Team. Estimate: 3.

Acceptance criteria:
  - Automated contract test passes in CI and prevents regressions to header passthrough.
  - Synthetic heartbeat runs every minute with tenant labels and has a per-tenant alert when missing two consecutive heartbeats.
  - Dashboards show tenant p95 ingress queue and a KV-eviction heatmap; at least two recent incidents can be attributed to tenants in staging.
  - Tracing sampling adjustments reduce loss of tenant-correlated spans to <1% during simulated ingress spikes.

Decision rationale & trade-offs: We deliberately avoid adding high-cardinality real-time tags to every metric (cost/ingest concerns); instead we (a) use tenant labels on a small set of critical synthetic metrics, (b) ensure trace correlation is robust, and (c) add a sparse aggregated tenant-percentile metric set to balance cardinality and visibility.

Rollout plan: land contract test + proxy defensive fallback on staging, run 48h canary with synthetic heartbeats enabled and runbook dry-run. Once stable, deploy to prod during low-traffic window (2026-03-18 02:00-04:00 UTC).

Monitoring & follow-ups: create an alert runbook entry, add a Grafana panel for "tenant attribution health" and add a SLO check that fail-fast if synthetic heartbeats drop for >5% tenants. Schedule a retro with product and on-call rotation to review runbook efficacy.

Artifacts & links: postmortem doc, incident timeline, and initial fixes are linked below.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Contract test in CI prevents header-drop regressions.
2) Per-tenant synthetic heartbeat present and alerting configured.
3) Tenant p95/p99 ingress queue and KV eviction heatmaps added to Console.
4) Sampling cliff addressed so trace-loss <1% under spike simulation.
